description: Address code review findings from PR #1 modernization

workflow.1-Review: Read files and understand current implementation
workflow.2-Evaluate: Is this valid, a false positive, or intentional design?
workflow.4-Implement: If fixing, make minimal focused changes
workflow.5-Document: Log decision and rationale to progress file

userStories.title: Consolidate duplicate build_structure_json function
userStories.description: The same function exists in two places: predict_table.py:64-120 and xlsx_exporter.py:172-228 (as build_xlsx_structure_from_extraction). Consolidate into one location and import where needed.
reviewQuestions: Are these functions actually identical or do they have subtle differences?
Is the duplication intentional to avoid circular imports?
Would consolidating create unwanted coupling between modules?
Are there different callers with different expectations?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Compare both functions side-by-side for differences
EVALUATE: Determine if consolidation is safe or if duplication is intentional
DECIDE: Document decision in progress file with rationale
IF FIXING: Single canonical function, both files import from it, all tests pass
IF SKIPPING: Document why duplication should remain (e.g., avoiding coupling)

userStories.title: Fix dead code in __main__ block
userStories.description: predict_table.py:925-928 has 'if __name__ == "__main__": detect_tables()' which will fail without arguments. Either add argparse for CLI usage or remove the dead code.
reviewQuestions: Is this __main__ block used for debugging/development?
Are there other scripts that call this file directly?
Would removing it break any workflows or documentation?
Is there value in making this a CLI tool?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Check if __main__ is referenced anywhere (scripts, docs, Makefile)
EVALUATE: Determine if CLI functionality would be useful or if it's truly dead code
DECIDE: Document decision in progress file with rationale
IF ADDING CLI: argparse with --pdf, --page, --help works correctly
IF REMOVING: Delete __main__ block, verify no breakage
IF KEEPING AS-IS: Document why (e.g., developer convenience placeholder)

userStories.title: Add multi-page PDF test coverage
userStories.description: PR checklist shows unchecked items for multi-page PDF extraction testing. Add integration tests that verify extraction works correctly across multiple pages.
reviewQuestions: Do existing tests already cover multi-page scenarios indirectly?
Is the multipage_table_pdf fixture in test_extractors.py sufficient?
What specific multi-page edge cases need coverage?
Is this a test gap or is multi-page tested elsewhere?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Search existing tests for multi-page coverage
EVALUATE: Identify actual test gaps vs already-covered scenarios
DECIDE: Document what tests are needed (if any) in progress file
IF ADDING TESTS: Cover pages with/without tables, correct page_num metadata
IF SUFFICIENT: Document why existing coverage is adequate

userStories.title: Improve exception handling specificity
userStories.description: Several places catch broad Exception and return empty results silently. Add logging and consider catching specific exceptions. Files: vision_extractor.py:132-134, camelot_extractor.py:125-130, pdfplumber_extractor.py:147-149.
reviewQuestions: Is catching broad Exception intentional for graceful degradation?
Would specific exceptions cause more harm (missed edge cases)?
Is logging already happening at a higher level?
Would adding logging create noise in normal operation?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Trace exception handling through the call stack
EVALUATE: Determine if broad catch is a valid design choice for resilience
DECIDE: Document decision in progress file with rationale
IF IMPROVING: Add logging, catch specific exceptions where safe
IF KEEPING: Document why broad exception handling is appropriate here

userStories.title: Optimize _score_regularity performance
userStories.description: scorer.py:257-261 uses df.iterrows() which is slow for large tables. Refactor to use vectorized pandas operations for better performance on large DataFrames.
reviewQuestions: How large are typical extracted tables? Is this actually a bottleneck?
Would vectorization make the code less readable?
Are there other iterrows() calls that should also be optimized?
Is premature optimization a concern here?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Check typical table sizes in real usage
EVALUATE: Benchmark current performance - is this actually slow?
DECIDE: Document decision in progress file with rationale
IF OPTIMIZING: Vectorize, verify same results, measure improvement
IF SKIPPING: Document why optimization isn't needed (e.g., tables are small)

userStories.title: Clean up unused parameters in extract_tables_vision
userStories.description: predict_table.py:867-870 extract_tables_vision() accepts flavor and row_tol parameters but never uses them. Either use them or document why they exist (API compatibility) more clearly.
reviewQuestions: Are these parameters for API consistency with extract_tables_direct?
Could future vision extractors use these parameters?
Would removing them break any callers?
Is the current comment sufficient documentation?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Check all callers of extract_tables_vision
EVALUATE: Determine if parameters serve API consistency purpose
DECIDE: Document decision in progress file with rationale
IF REMOVING: Update all callers, verify no breakage
IF KEEPING: Add clear docstring explaining they're for API compatibility

userStories.title: Document magic numbers in scorer.py
userStories.description: scorer.py has several unexplained constants: weight tolerance 0.01 (line 68), text capture multiplier 2 and ratio 0.7/0.3 (line 215), structure weights (lines 270-274). Add comments explaining the rationale.
reviewQuestions: Are these values empirically tuned or arbitrary?
Would extracting to named constants reduce readability?
Is this over-documentation for self-evident values?
Do similar libraries use similar values?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Understand what each constant does and why
EVALUATE: Determine if documentation adds value or is noise
DECIDE: Document decision in progress file with rationale
IF DOCUMENTING: Add concise comments explaining rationale
IF SKIPPING: Document why values are self-evident or standard

userStories.title: Add missing type annotations
userStories.description: Some functions lack complete type annotations. Add type hints to: collect_result() at table_extract.py:574, collect_parsing_report() at line 594, and other untyped parameters.
reviewQuestions: Is the codebase consistently typed or mostly untyped?
Would adding types to just these functions be inconsistent?
Are these internal functions that don't need strict typing?
Would this trigger a larger typing effort?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Assess typing consistency across codebase
EVALUATE: Determine if selective typing adds value or creates inconsistency
DECIDE: Document decision in progress file with rationale
IF ADDING: Add accurate type hints that would pass mypy
IF SKIPPING: Document why (e.g., codebase isn't typed, would be inconsistent)

userStories.title: Consolidate flavor auto-detection logic
userStories.description: Both detect_tables() (YOLO path) and MultiExtractor have similar logic for comparing lattice vs stream extraction results. Consider extracting this into a shared utility function.
reviewQuestions: Are the two implementations actually similar or subtly different?
Would a shared utility create unwanted coupling?
Is the duplication acceptable for code clarity?
Would refactoring make the code harder to follow?
acceptanceCriteria: REVIEW: Compare both implementations side-by-side
EVALUATE: Determine if consolidation improves or harms maintainability
DECIDE: Document decision in progress file with rationale
IF CONSOLIDATING: Extract shared utility, update both callers, all tests pass
IF SKIPPING: Document why separation is preferred (e.g., different contexts)

phases.1: High Priority - Must fix before merge

decisionTypes.FIX: Issue is valid, implementing the fix
decisionTypes.SKIP: Issue is a false positive or intentional design choice
decisionTypes.ALTERNATIVE: Issue is valid but implementing a different solution
decisionTypes.DEFER: Issue is valid but should be addressed separately
